key_insight: Human and LLM recipe generation performed comparably in closed-loop materials synthesis, and together they enabled discovery of a new material, Ba3PtO5, with a previously unknown structural prototype.
engineering_relevance: The study shows that pairing LLMs with experimental feedback can accelerate synthesis planning and expand the search space for new functional materials beyond known structures.
method: Generated synthesis recipes for known and unknown Ruddlesden-Popper-related materials using both humans and LLMs
Tested the recipes in-lab and fed outcomes back into a closed-loop collaboration process
Compared success rates across two rounds and used the workflow to identify a new material
evidence_signal: The abstract reports measured synthesis success rates from in-lab experiments across two rounds, with humans and LLMs showing similar performance on known and unknown targets.
watch_item: Success rates were much lower for unknown materials than for known ones, so real-world deployment still depends on careful experimental validation and domain expertise.
paper_title: Human and LLM Collaboration for Accelerated Materials Synthesis and Discovery
